name: alarm_net_fault
notes: bring-up failed or the link was lost; check the cable, the switch and net_ip

name: alarm_ntp_timeout
notes: the wall clock is free-running: anything dated, scheduled or solar is adrift

name: alarm_log_flood
notes: the rate limiter is shedding; something is repeating itself and the record is incomplete

name: alarm_flash_error
notes: parameters will not survive a reboot; check the KV region

name: alarm_fieldbus
desc: a field device is not answering
notes: check the RS-485 wiring, termination and the device's own power

name: alarm_scan_late
desc: a control program is missing its period
notes: check the TASKS page and the per-program cost; something is overrunning or the site asks for more than the beat holds

name: alarm_fieldbus_line
desc: the whole segment has gone quiet
notes: the trunk, the termination, this unit's transceiver, or a second master - not twenty devices that failed at once

name: alarm_io_drop
desc: a field row is never scanned
notes: the planner could not place it: the device model's limits, or more rows than the plan holds. It is a signal that will never be read

name: sys_fieldbus_dead
notes: 0 when every planned device is talking

name: sys_fieldbus_crc
notes: rising means the line: termination, stub length, or the wrong baud

name: sys_fieldbus_stray
desc: bytes that arrived out of turn
notes: rising means a second master, a duplicate address, or a device answering after its turn had passed

lead:
/* The scan CLOCK, not an elapsed time. A C++ law is handed dt through
* ProgramContext; ST has no argument to be handed anything, so a block
* reads this and keeps its own last value. That makes it rate-independent
* - the same block works on any task - and it is the simulator's VIRTUAL
* clock, so accelerated time works unchanged.
* Wraps at 2^32 ms, about 49 days: unsigned subtraction carries it, and
* no block goes that long between scans.
* Gated on PLC, which is what reads it. It sat under the RS-485 client's
* guard, where a build with programs and no field bus lost the clock and
* every ST timer resolved to the inert sink. */
name: sys_now_ms
desc: the scan clock, milliseconds since boot
notes: ST blocks difference it themselves; wraps at ~49 days and unsigned subtraction carries it

lead:
/* The DATE, for a law that counts in days rather than in milliseconds.
* Straight off the wall clock and NOT through cal_time_ms(), which takes
* an UPTIME instant and projects it onto the wall: handing it a wall time
* adds the boot epoch twice, and the date came out around 2083 and gained
* a day every twelve hours. 0 is "the RTC has never been set", which is
* a real answer and the one a schedule refuses to run against. */
name: sys_today
desc: days since 1 Jan 1970, 0 before the clock is set
notes: the wall clock as a DATE; a schedule counts in these and cannot run on 0

name: sol_ready
desc: the solar tracker has a location and a clock
notes: one row, not one per solar output: they all go together, and every boot passes through this until NTP lands

name: sol_fromRise_min
desc: minutes since sunrise; negative before it
notes: what the sol_ phase offsets are measured against

name: sol_fromSet_min
desc: minutes since sunset; negative before it
notes: held until the tracker has a location and a wall clock

name: sol_elev_deg
desc: the sun's elevation above the horizon
notes: negative below it; what the day's shape is anticipated from

name: monitor_log_level
desc: lowest level the monitor port carries
notes: open by default: this port exists to be the full record

notes: 0=VT100 1=VT102 2=Minitel 1B 3=Minitel 2

name: console_rows

notes: `logs off` silences it entirely without moving this
label: &Logs::level_label

desc: lowest level the LOGS page keeps
notes: this page is the record; raising it loses the record
label: &Logs::level_label

name: sys_cpu_load_pct
notes: percent of the task period

name: sys_jitter_pct
notes: percent of the task period

name: sys_stack_pct
notes: percent of the stack in use

name: sys_startup_sec
notes: nothing runs a law on a field that has not answered yet; 0 runs from the first beat

name: sys_control
notes: off stops every law and drops what they were driving to its declared safe state; per-program is `programs disable`

name: sys_shutdown_sec
desc: laws stopped before the ending, seconds
notes: the mirror of sys_startup_sec: time for the record to reach flash before a reset

name: sys_retain_sec
desc: how often retained values reach flash
notes: 0 leaves only `save` and the way down; wear vs loss

name: rtu_timeout_ms
desc: how long a slave has to answer
notes: the bus default; a device model may declare its own

name: rtu_retries
desc: immediate retries before a device is backed off
notes: each costs a full timeout on a device that is really gone

name: rtu_backoff_ms
desc: first backoff after a device fails its retries
notes: doubles per further failure, up to rtu_backoff_max_ms

name: rtu_backoff_max_ms
desc: longest a backed-off device waits between probes
notes: what decides whether one dead device costs the whole bus

name: rtu_write_min_ms
desc: shortest interval between writes to one block
notes: what stops a chattering demand monopolising the bus

name: rtu_rewrite_ms
desc: how often an output block is written anyway
notes: MATCH the slave's own failsafe timer; it is watching for this
